newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on weather outlook, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on weather outlook, exports.

text.p: Outlooks for improved harvest weather in the U.S. Midwest plus slack exports pressured CBOT corn futures at midsession, traders said.

"Corn is still overpriced. There's not enough demand to match the supply and that's all it boils down too," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago trade house FIMAT Futures. "Nobody is short corn and there's no reason to buy it right now."
USDA Thursday confirmed in its weekly export sales report that U.S. corn export sales have been lagging plus technical traders cited a continuation of a bearish slide.
December corn Friday traded in a narrow 2-3/4 cents per bushel range with the session high at $2.77-3/4 and the low at $2.75.

Technicians cited first support in the December at $2.76-1/4 and resistance at $281.1/4. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 24 points which is considered a short term oversold mark.
Traders said they expected U.S. corn harvesting to speed up now that over two-thirds of the soy crop has been combined.
Corn closed one to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 2-3/4 at $2.75-1/4.

Key players included Griffin Trading with two million bushels sold in the December, traders said. Lehman Bros bought two million bushels of December, Cargill Inc bought one million December and sold 1.5 million March, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 55,000, down from 75,001 Thursday.

In corn options, Credit Agricole bought 1,000 March $2.70 puts and sold 1,000 December $2.70 puts, LFG Futures sold 500 March $2.70 puts at seven cents and Produce Grain bought 500 December $2.70 puts at 2-3/4 to 3-3/4 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000, down from 18,685 Thursday.
